title: Electrician Software: 7 Tools for Service Calls and Project Jobs
html:
Electrician software splits into two camps: apps built for service calls and apps built for project jobs. A shop that runs panel swaps and repairs needs a quick quote and invoice tool. A shop that bids new construction needs job costing. Pair either with electrician SEO so calls keep coming. Published prices in this guide run from $14 to $399 a month.

Electrician software has to match the way you earn money. A service electrician books a dozen small tickets a week and wants speed. A contractor bidding a tenant buildout runs a few large jobs and wants budgets, change orders and cost tracking. Buying the wrong type means paying for features you never open.

This guide covers seven tools, the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each. It starts with the apps for service work, moves to project tools, and ends with the free listing that brings in calls. The tools are tested only on what the vendor's own page says.

Which electrician software suits a shop that sells service calls?

Joist, Jobber and Housecall Pro all target small field crews that quote, schedule and invoice. They differ most in price and in how many users you get.

  • Joist: Basics is limited to up to 5 documents a month. Pro lists unlimited documents at $17 a month billed monthly, or $14.17 effective when billed annually. Limit: the page shows several unlabeled prices for other plans, so confirm each one with Joist before you buy.
  • Jobber: Core for 1 user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Extra users on higher plans cost $29 a month each. Limit: card processing is 2.9% plus 30 cents, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are billed on top.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually for 1 user, and Essentials is $149 annual for 5 users. Max is $299 annual for 8 users. Limit: Basic has one user, and several add-ons have no price on the page.

A one-man electrician fits Joist Pro or Jobber Core. A crew of five fits Housecall Pro Essentials, which lists 5 users for $149 a month billed annually. The page also lists QuickBooks Online sync on that plan, which saves retyping invoices.

Seats are the hidden cost for crews with helpers. Helpers who only upload photos may not need a paid seat. JobTread says field crew who only upload photos and notes are free. Other vendors count users differently, so ask who counts before you add the whole crew.

Pricing models also affect how you hire. Per-user plans such as Housecall Pro and Jobber add cost with every new office seat. A flat plan like Knowify Advanced covers ten users, so the tenth hire costs nothing extra until you pass that limit.

Service electricians quote fast and often. Build a template for each repeat job, such as a panel upgrade, a ceiling fan install or an EV charger. Whatever app you use, the quote should go out before you leave the driveway.

Which electrician business software gives a quote on request?

FieldPulse is a field service platform that asks you to request a custom quote. It is the one tool in this guide with no published price.

  • FieldPulse: the page says pricing is seat-based and built around what your team needs. Its Engage phone system is billed by line and license, and an AI assistant called Maverick is included on all plans. Limit: no plan names, dollar amounts or seat counts appear, so you cannot budget without talking to sales.

Treat a quote-only vendor as a second round. Gather the published prices first, set your budget, then ask FieldPulse to match your headcount in writing. If the quote lands far above the published tools, you have your answer.

What free tool gets an electrician found for urgent calls?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows an electrician in Google Maps when a homeowner searches for an electrician nearby. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, phone number, hours and reviews. Limit: it only helps when the address is accurate and the profile gets fresh photos, posts and review replies.

Urgent electrical calls, such as a dead outlet or a tripped main, are searched on a phone. A call button and correct hours decide who gets the call.

JobberService crews$29 to $49 a month for CoreExtra users cost more
Housecall ProService crews up to 8 users$59 to $299 a month, billed annuallyAdd-ons not priced
JobTreadProject jobs$199 a month plus $20 per userNo free trial
KnowifyProject jobs with budgets$329 to $399 a monthCore lacks project budgets
FieldPulseQuote-only tradesNot publishedNeeds a sales call
Google Business ProfileMap listingFreeNeeds steady upkeep

How much does electrician software cost for a five-person shop?

A five-person electrical shop that mostly sells service calls has clear published options. Housecall Pro Essentials is $149 a month billed annually for 5 users. Jobber charges $49 for Core with one user, so five people need a higher plan with $29 extra users. Joist Pro is $17 for one account.

A five-person shop that bids projects pays $279 a month on JobTread with monthly billing. Knowify Advanced starts at $329 and includes ten users. Neither includes accounting software, card fees or add-ons.

Card processing can change the math. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, and Housecall Pro says rates start as low as 2.59%. On a $2,400 panel upgrade, one percentage point is $24. Ask every vendor for the rate on your typical ticket.

What should you ask an electrician software vendor before you sign?

Ask five questions in the demo and write down the answers. Vendors change plans often, so a written answer beats the page you read today.

Test with a real job. Take last month's biggest project and enter its budget, then enter a small service call. If either takes too long, move on. Housecall Pro offers a 14-day trial on Max, and Jobber offers a 14-day trial of Grow.

What does electrician software not do for you?

Electrician software tracks the work you already won. It does not rank your website, run ads or fill a slow month, and none of the tools above does those things.

Your website needs service pages, a call button and a form that reaches your job tool. It is a managed build, not a template you edit yourself.

How do you choose electrician software for your company?

Choose electrician software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: is most of your revenue from service tickets or from bid projects, and does the tool handle that work first?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, card fees and add-ons, then compare the total with your average job.

Setup effort: can the office import customers and a price list in a week, or does it need paid onboarding?

A solo electrician can run on Joist Pro or Jobber Core and a free Google Business Profile. A service crew of five fits Housecall Pro Essentials. A contractor bidding projects fits JobTread or Knowify. A shop that does both should pick the app for its larger revenue line and handle the other in a spreadsheet until it grows.

Plan the rollout in three steps. Week one, enter open jobs and your standard price list. Week two, build templates for your five most common jobs. Week three, move invoicing into the app and stop the old paper process. Cancel inside the trial or first month if the crew is not using it.

Software works hardest when calls keep coming. For a related trade, read the handyman software guide.

What software does an electrician need?

An electrician needs a way to quote jobs, schedule work and take payment. A contractor who bids projects also needs job costing and budgets. Every electrician needs a Google Business Profile so customers can find the company. Start with the type of work that earns most of your revenue.

How much does electrician software cost?

Published plans here run from $14.17 a month for Joist Pro billed annually to $399 a month for Knowify Advanced. JobTread is $199 a month plus $20 per extra user. FieldPulse publishes no price. Card fees and add-ons cost more, so confirm the total for your crew.

Is JobTread or Knowify better for an electrical contractor?

Both suit contractors who bid projects. JobTread lists $199 a month plus $20 per extra user, with unlimited jobs. Knowify lists Advanced at $329 or $399 a month with 10 users included. Compare both at your headcount and the features you will use.

Can a small electrician use Jobber or Housecall Pro?

Yes, for scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments. Jobber lists Core at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists Basic at $59 a month billed annually. Both fit service work, but project budgets are better handled by a job costing tool.

Does FieldPulse publish its prices?

No. The FieldPulse says pricing is seat-based and asks you to request a custom quote. It lists no plan names or dollar amounts. Ask for a written quote at your headcount and compare it with the published prices of other tools.

Is Google Business Profile free for an electrician?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: accurate service areas, photos of finished jobs and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products, such as Local Service Ads, are separate and carry their own costs.

What should a new electrician buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first, because calls come before dispatch. Then add one quote and invoice app that fits your headcount. Move to job costing only when you start bidding projects that need budgets.
